cues.zh: 有些代码可能会请求它，所以它们必须……这些信息必须存在。

cues.en: And those optimizations are really... I will characterize... They would probably disagree, but I will characterize as they're digging ourselves out of a hole that we already jumped into.
cues.zh: 而那些优化其实……我这么形容吧……他们大概不会同意，但我会说，这就像我们已经在坑里了，还在把自己往外挖。

cues.en: Just a suggestion,
cues.zh: 只是个建议，

cues.en: how about not jumping into the hole
cues.zh: 不如别一见洞就往里跳

cues.en: unless we need the information, unless we need the... We know there's treasure right here in the field instead of digging up the whole field and jumping into every hole. Oh, no, only the time that we need to get the treasure chest. We'll go and we'll dig there. We'll opt in.
cues.zh: 除非我们真需要那条信息，除非我们真需要……我们知道宝藏就在这片地里，而不是把整片地都挖开、每个洞都跳进去。哦不，只有在我们需要拿到宝箱的时候，才去那里挖。我们按需选择加入。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: so a pay for what you use principle
cues.zh: 所以是“用多少付多少”的原则

cues.en: to keep in mind for the rest of the talk,
cues.zh: 接下来的分享里请记住这一点，

cues.en: make things static,
cues.zh: 让东西变成静态的，

cues.en: compile time
cues.zh: 编译期

cues.en: by default.
cues.zh: 默认如此。

cues.en: And dynamic is still there. We're not taking anything away from you,
cues.zh: 动态特性仍然还在。我们不会从你那里拿走任何东西，

cues.en: But it's only if you ask for it. And make it easy to ask for it, make it convenient,
cues.zh: 但只有你主动要求时才会有。并且要让它容易请求、用起来方便，

cues.en: but dynamic by opt in. Static by default, dynamic by opt in.
cues.zh: 但动态特性要靠主动选择。默认静态，动态靠主动选择。

cues.en: So let's take a look at the first part of the talk, which is about exception handling.
cues.zh: 那么我们先看演讲的第一部分，也就是异常处理。

cues.en: The first thing to do is establish the problem. Then we'll talk about what is an error for a couple of slides just to make sure we know... Have in our minds what a runtime error is.
cues.zh: 首先要明确问题。然后我们会用几页幻灯片讨论什么是错误，只是为了确保我们知道……心里清楚运行时错误是什么。

cues.en: And then I'll show the proposals that I'm bringing forward. And again, I should put a disclaimer here. I do chair the Standards Committee, but this is just me talking as an individual. The standards committee may or may not like any of this. I'm not speaking for them.
cues.zh: 接下来我会介绍自己提出的提案。这里得先声明一下：我确实担任标准委员会主席，但以下只代表我个人观点。标准委员会未必认同这些内容，我不代表他们发言。

cues.en: But as I go through the talk, in a couple of places, I will show straw poll results as to what the committee does think, and I'll put context in it from the Cologne meeting two months ago about this proposal where it was seen for the first time in the full language evolution working group.
cues.zh: 不过在演讲过程中，有几处我会展示委员会真实意见的民意测验结果，并补充两个月前科隆会议的相关背景——当时这个提案首次在全语言演进工作组面前亮相。

cues.en: But let's now first establish the problem. Let's say we have this function. What do you think of this code? Just shout it out.
cues.zh: 不过我们先来把问题明确一下。假设我们有这个函数。你们觉得这段代码怎么样？直接喊出来。

cues.en: Two forms of error handling.
cues.zh: 两种错误处理形式。

cues.en: Something unprintable, I think, but I couldn't quite hear.
cues.zh: 我觉得是某种说不出口的东西，但我没太听清。

cues.en: A fireable offense perhaps? Maybe not quite that bad.
cues.zh: 也许该被开除？可能也没那么严重。

cues.en: But it's like driving,
cues.zh: 但这就像开车，

cues.en: you're behind a driver who's white lining it and drifting a little, and your choices are
cues.zh: 你跟在一位压着白线、还有点跑偏的司机后面，而你的选择是

cues.en: stay behind them because you can't pass on the left or on the right or call 911. They probably want to consider the latter
cues.zh: 继续跟在他们后面，因为你不能从左边或右边超车，也不能打 911。他们大概想考虑后者

cues.en: if you're in most countries. In some countries, this is normal, they know what to do.
cues.zh: 如果你在大多数国家。在某些国家，这很正常，他们知道该怎么做。

cues.en: But they haven't decided. The author of this function hasn't made a decision that the author of a function has
cues.zh: 但他们还没决定。这个函数的作者还没做出决定，而函数作者有

cues.en: a duty to make.
cues.zh: 责任去做出这个决定。

cues.en: When I design a function or a class,
cues.zh: 当我设计一个函数或一个类时，

cues.en: part of my responsibility
cues.zh: 我的一部分责任

cues.en: as a designer
cues.zh: 作为设计者

cues.en: is to specify the error handling and decide on the error handling policy.
cues.zh: 就是明确错误处理，并决定错误处理策略。

cues.en: Here, if I say, yeah, sometimes we'll throw something, sometimes we'll return something, I have abdicated my responsibility
cues.zh: 在这里，如果我说，对，有时我们会抛出异常，有时我们会返回结果，那我就推卸了我的责任

cues.en: as a designer.
cues.zh: 作为设计者。

cues.en: Now what's harder than getting your caller to do error handling? Getting them to do it twice
cues.zh: 还有什么比让调用方做错误处理更难的？让他们做两次。

cues.en: in two ways. Now this is a real problem because today we are bifurcated.
cues.zh: 用两种方式。现在这确实是个问题，因为如今我们已经分裂成两套了。

cues.en: Some libraries may return a widget error. Some libraries may return... May throw an exception. And how am I ever going to write templated code that can call either of these and do something sensible? Because in one case, even if this
cues.zh: 有些库可能返回 widget 错误。有些库可能返回……可能抛出异常。那我到底要怎么写出模板代码，既能调用其中任意一种，又能做出合理处理？因为在一种情况下，即使这个

cues.en: function,
cues.zh: 函数，

cues.en: this template doesn't handle the error,
cues.zh: 这个模板不处理错误，

cues.en: Just to propagate it, it has to know, do I do nothing and let the exception propagate, because that's nice and automatic? Or do I have to say if error, return error?
cues.zh: 仅仅为了传播它，它就必须知道：我是该什么都不做，让异常继续传播，因为这样又简单又自动？还是必须写成 if error, return error？

cues.en: I don't know.
cues.zh: 我不知道。

cues.en: This is also an example why not agreeing on a common error handling policy means I am effectively bifurcating the community. I am effectively programming in a language dialect, an incompatible one, because I can't compose these two libraries easily
cues.zh: 这也是个例子，说明为什么在错误处理策略上达不成共识，实际上会让社区分裂。我实际上是在用一种语言方言编程，一种不兼容的方言，因为我没法轻松地把这两个库组合起来

cues.en: in cases like this.
cues.zh: 在这种情况下。

cues.en: So I took a survey,
cues.zh: 所以我做了一项调查，

cues.en: and this is part of the isocpp.org
cues.zh: 这是 isocpp.org 的

cues.en: survey. I talked about this when I gave this talk, this part of the talk at ACCU this spring.
cues.zh: 调查的一部分。我在今年春天 ACCU 上讲这个演讲时谈到过这一点，也就是演讲的这一部分。

cues.en: And about half of C plus plus projects ban exceptions in whole or in part. And these are the numbers from about eighteen months ago. There was another survey done about
cues.zh: 大约一半的 C++ 项目会全部或部分禁用异常。这些是大约 18 个月前的数据。还有一项调查是在大约

cues.en: 12 ago.
cues.zh: 12 个月前做的。

cues.en: Notice the numbers are very much the same.
cues.zh: 注意，这些数字几乎一样。

cues.en: And then the most recent one, which was done this spring,
cues.zh: 然后是最近一次调查，今年春天做的，

cues.en: the good news is there are now... And and this could be measurement error. We'll keep measuring this. But there are 3% more. Notice we went from 49 to 52%. 3% more that allow exceptions everywhere. But you might have noticed there are also 3% more that say they're banned completely.
cues.zh: 好消息是现在……这可能是测量误差。我们会继续测量。但多了 3%。注意我们从 49% 到了 52%。全面允许异常的多了 3%。不过你可能也注意到，声称完全禁用异常的也多了 3%。

cues.en: So that is not improvement.
cues.zh: 所以这不是改进。

cues.en: That is further bifurcation.
cues.zh: 这是进一步分化。

cues.en: You're getting less middle ground and more
cues.zh: 中间地带越来越少，更多的是

cues.en: the polar ends.
cues.zh: 两极。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: that's a shame because if we ban exceptions,
cues.zh: 这很遗憾，因为如果我们禁用异常，

cues.en: we're not using c plus plus And
cues.zh: 我们用的就不是 C++ 了。而且

cues.en: as I said at ACC, that may sound like an ideological statement, but I think it's a factual one, not ideological.
cues.zh: 正如我在 ACC 上说的，这听起来可能像意识形态论断，但我认为它是事实判断，不是意识形态。

cues.en: We're not using standard c plus plus because standard c plus plus requires the constructors that fail throw an exception. There is no other reasonable way to report errors, and it's what the standard library does. If you overload an operator,
cues.zh: 我们用的不是标准 C++，因为标准 C++ 要求失败的构造函数抛出异常。没有其他合理的错误报告方式，标准库就是这么做的。如果你重载一个运算符，

cues.en: there's no space in the signature. The signature is defined by the language. If you're operator plus, you take two things and return nothing. Where do you stick an error code?
cues.zh: 签名里没有空间。签名是由语言定义的。如果是 operator+，你接收两个东西，返回一个结果。错误码往哪儿塞？

cues.en: You you can't.
cues.zh: 你……你做不到。

cues.en: So if you're in an f no exceptions world, you're not using constructors, you're using factory functions, generally,
cues.zh: 所以在 -fno-exceptions 的世界里，你一般不会用构造函数，而是用工厂函数，

cues.en: if they can fail. If they can fail, you're not using operator overloading, you're using named functions.
cues.zh: 前提是它们可能失败。如果它们可能失败，你就不会用运算符重载，而是用具名函数。

cues.en: You're likely not using the standard library,
cues.zh: 你很可能也不会用标准库，

cues.en: except maybe for the algorithms, because they generally don't throw.
cues.zh: 也许算法除外，因为它们一般不会抛异常。

cues.en: Especially if you've disabled bad alloc, most library functions, standard library algorithms don't throw.
cues.zh: 尤其是如果你禁用了 bad_alloc，大多数库函数和标准库算法都不会抛异常。

cues.en: But you're not using the containers, at least not the standard ones. You may be in a divergent version of the STL that's not compatible,
cues.zh: 但你没用这些容器，至少不是标准那套。你可能处在某个分叉的 STL 版本里，它不兼容，

cues.en: that does something else when
cues.zh: 它在以下情况下会做别的事：

cues.en: exception handling is turned off.
cues.zh: 异常处理被关闭时。

cues.en: And this is fragmentation.
cues.zh: 这就是碎片化。

cues.en: Interestingly, when you take these same numbers and you look at them by the three kinds of error reporting that we pulled, which was exceptions,
cues.zh: 有意思的是，把这些同样的数字按我们提取出的三类错误报告方式来分别看——也就是异常、

cues.en: numeric error codes, and sort of expected outcome result style types.
cues.zh: 数字错误码，以及那种 expected、outcome 风格的结果类型。

cues.en: One of the most interesting data points I found is that error codes have the strongest support of those three.
cues.zh: 我发现最有趣的数据点之一是，错误码在这三者中支持度最高。

cues.en: That's
cues.zh: 也就是说

cues.en: the community voting with their feet.
cues.zh: 社区在用脚投票。

cues.en: The expected outcome types, are totally non standard,
cues.zh: 预期结果类型完全不标准，

cues.en: even though some of them are in boost, many of them are custom,
cues.zh: 虽然其中一些在 boost 里，但很多都是自定义的，

cues.en: are allowed everywhere almost as much as exceptions which are blessed in the C plus plus standard and have language support.
cues.zh: 它们几乎和异常一样被到处允许使用，而异常是 C++ 标准所认可的，并且有语言层面的支持。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: perhaps most disturbingly,
cues.zh: 也许最令人不安的是，

cues.en: every one of these is banned outright in more than 10% of projects according to these surveys.
cues.zh: 根据这些调查，这些做法中的每一种都在超过 10% 的项目中被彻底禁止。

cues.en: And that is a measure of how fragmented
cues.zh: 这衡量出世界已经变得

cues.en: the world has become because that means there are projects that cannot talk to each other at all, that cannot share code
cues.zh: 多么碎片化，因为这意味着有些项目完全无法互通、无法共享代码

cues.en: at all, at least not code that does error handling, and I
cues.zh: 完全不能，至少不能共享做错误处理的代码，而我

cues.en: hope that most of our code does or aspires to.
cues.zh: 希望我们大多数代码都能做到，或者正朝这个方向努力。

cues.en: When you look at these same numbers, there's the original, there's six months later, and here's the most recent one from this year, you see a very similar pattern.
cues.zh: 看看这些相同的数字：有最初的，有六个月后的，还有今年最新的，你会看到非常相似的模式。

cues.en: So this is pretty stable across
cues.zh: 所以这一点相当稳定，在各项

cues.en: surveys.
cues.zh: 调查中。

cues.en: So standard C plus plus says we have exceptions enabled. We use constructors and operators normally. We use the standard template library.
cues.zh: 所以标准 C++ 说我们启用了异常。我们正常使用构造函数和运算符。我们使用标准模板库。

cues.en: And then there's dialects. And there's not just one. There are many of them because we keep inventing new ways to not use exceptions and to report errors some other way.
cues.zh: 然后是各种方言。而且不止一种。有很多种，因为我们不断发明新方法，来避开异常，并用其他方式报告错误。

cues.en: And question, which of these does std file system use? And the answer is two of them.
cues.zh: 问题是，std::filesystem 用的是其中哪些？答案是其中两个。

cues.en: So throughout the now standard file system library,
cues.zh: 所以在如今标准的文件系统库里，

cues.en: pervasively there are overloads,
cues.zh: 到处都有重载，

cues.en: one of which will return an error and one of which will throw an exception just in case you're in one of those worlds. The
cues.zh: 其中一个返回错误，另一个抛出异常，以防你处在那种世界里。而

cues.en: C plus plus community is so bifurcated
cues.zh: C++ 社区如此分裂，

cues.en: that the standards committee
cues.zh: 以至于标准委员会

cues.en: feels they need to support both of these dialects, and they will probably not say it in those terms, but I will.
cues.zh: 觉得需要同时支持这两种方言；他们大概不会这么说，但我会。

cues.en: We are supporting what is effectively becoming two languages, and that is not a good thing. And we have pressure to do this with our next round of libraries
cues.zh: 我们实际上在支持正在变成两种语言的东西，这不是好事。而且我们面临压力，要在下一批库里也这么做

cues.en: like networking and other libraries that are coming to do the same thing
cues.zh: 比如网络库和其他即将做同样事情的库

cues.en: just so c plus plus developers can use them.
cues.zh: 只是为了 C++ 开发者能用它们。

cues.en: That's a problem that needs a solution. And what's the root cause?
cues.zh: 这是一个需要解决的问题。那根本原因是什么？

cues.en: Today's exception handling is not zero overhead.
cues.zh: 如今的异常处理并不是零开销。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: summarizing the reasons as I've gone and surveyed people and teams over the last five years or so,
cues.zh: 总结一下我过去五年左右调研个人和团队时听到的原因，

cues.en: and longer than that, but especially systematically in the last five years, I've been hearing the same three things over and over, two things and then an optional one. The first is I can't turn on exception handling at all. And you ask them, why? It's standard. We recommend it. It's beautiful.
cues.zh: 其实时间更长，但尤其是过去五年系统地调研下来，我反复听到同样的三件事，两件是必有的，还有一件是可选的。第一是我根本没法开启异常处理。你问他们为什么？这是标准做法。我们推荐它。它很优雅。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: look what it costs. And they show binary size, or they show other expense of it. Because just turning on exception handling incurs space overhead on every implementation, whether you throw anything or not. And this is regardless of whether you're using table based exceptions or non table based exceptions. It is even with the optimizations
cues.zh: 看看它的代价。他们展示了二进制体积，或者展示了其他开销。因为仅仅开启异常处理，就会在每种实现上带来空间开销，不管你实际有没有抛出异常。而且无论你用的是基于表的异常还是非基于表的异常，都是如此。即便是采用了那些

cues.en: that have been proposed and reported in this year's standards committee failings.
cues.zh: 今年标准委员会会议上已经提出并报告过的优化，也仍然如此。

cues.en: And this violates the first part of the zero overhead principle, which was you don't pay for what you don't use.
cues.zh: 这就违反了零开销原则的第一部分：你没用到的，就不该付出代价。

cues.en: I should be able to turn on exception handling, and if I don't throw an exception, I should pay approximately zero.
cues.zh: 我应该能开启异常处理，而只要我不抛异常，开销就应该是零。

cues.en: A nice round number. And we're not there today.
cues.zh: 一个漂亮的整数。而今天我们还做不到。

cues.en: The second problem is, okay, even if I have enabled,
cues.zh: 第二个问题是，好吧，即使我已经开启了，

cues.en: in certain code I may not be able to throw an exception, and you ask them, well, why? And there's two sub reasons for this one.
cues.zh: 在某些代码里我可能还是不能抛异常，你问他们为什么，这有两个子原因。

cues.en: In real time systems
cues.zh: 在实时系统中

cues.en: or memory constrained
cues.zh: 或内存受限的

cues.en: systems,
cues.zh: 系统中，

cues.en: where they have to be able to predict for a call tree including
cues.zh: 他们必须能够预测一棵调用树的

cues.en: for reporting an error how much space and or how much time
cues.zh: 包括报告错误时，需要多少空间和/或多少时间

cues.en: it will maximally take. So compute an upper bound on either space or time, or in some cases both.
cues.zh: 它最多会占用多少。因此要计算空间或时间，或某些情况下两者的上界。

cues.en: Can't throw an exception because I cannot statically compute an upper bound for how much space or time might be needed. And it's because I have to do dynamic allocation to throw and a form of RTTI to catch.
cues.zh: 不能抛出异常，因为我无法静态计算出可能需要的空间或时间的上界。这是因为我必须进行动态分配才能抛出，并且需要某种形式的 RTTI 才能捕获。

cues.en: Even if they're not in that kind of constrained system where the performance of an... The deterministic performance of exceptions
cues.zh: 即使它们不在那种受限的系统里，也就是异常在确定性性能方面表现很关键的系统

cues.en: is important,
cues.zh: 这一点很重要，

cues.en: they may say, yeah, I could throw. But look, I returned an expected. And I can prove it's a 100 times faster in my scenario.
cues.zh: 他们可能会说，是啊，我可以抛出异常。但你看，我返回了一个 expected，而且我能证明在我的场景里它快了 100 倍。

cues.en: And that may matter even when people say, well, you know, you should throw exceptions only in exceptional circumstances.
cues.zh: 而这一点可能很重要，即使人们说，你知道的，你只应该在异常情况下抛出异常。

cues.en: We're gonna get a better definition in a few minutes. But that's not always true. You need to throw an exception when the function couldn't do what it advertised, and that usually is rare,
cues.zh: 几分钟后我们会给出一个更好的定义。但这并不总是成立。当函数无法做到它所承诺的事情时，你就需要抛出异常，而这通常很罕见，

cues.en: but there are some functions
cues.zh: 但有些函数

cues.en: that actually may fail often, and that is a legitimate
cues.zh: 确实可能经常失败，而那是一种合理的

cues.en: failure.
cues.zh: 失败。

cues.en: Imagine parsing XML or
cues.zh: 想象一下解析 XML，或者

cues.en: Let's for a moment define what is an error. If you go to the dictionary, Marriott Webster's a good one. They define error as an act that fails to achieve what should be done. So if you call a function that says
cues.zh: 我们先来定义一下什么是错误。查字典的话，Merriam-Webster 是个不错的选择。他们把错误定义为未能达成应有目标的行为。所以如果你调用一个函数，比如

cues.en: parse int and you pass it a string,
cues.zh: parse int，然后传给它一个字符串，

cues.en: if it can't get you an integer out of that string, then it can't achieve what you asked it to do. That's a simple example.
cues.zh: 如果它无法从这个字符串中解析出整数，那它就没能完成你要求它做的事。这是个简单的例子。

cues.en: Basically, comes down to can the function achieve its success post conditions? Can it do the thing it advertises?
cues.zh: 基本上，归根结底就是：这个函数能否达成它的成功后置条件？它能不能做到它宣称的事？

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: I'll say let's use the term error, and to be CRISPR, a recoverable error, a program recoverable error,
cues.zh: 我想说，我们用“错误”这个词，说得明确一点，是可恢复的错误，程序层面可恢复的错误，

cues.en: means a function couldn't do what it advertised.
cues.zh: 意思是函数做不到它宣称的事。

cues.en: Only
cues.zh: 只有

cues.en: those
cues.zh: 那些

cues.en: should be reported as errors to the caller. And notice I did not say anything about it, whether you use exceptions or result types or error codes.
cues.zh: 才应该作为错误报告给调用方。注意，我完全没提你是用异常、结果类型还是错误码。

cues.en: This is a very general principle that doesn't... That is agnostic
cues.zh: 这是一条非常通用的原则，它不……也就是说，它不依赖于

cues.en: to the actual mechanism you use to report the error. Is you shouldn't even be telling the calling code about it unless it's in this category.
cues.zh: 你用来报告错误的实际机制。而且，除非属于这一类，否则你甚至不应该把这件事告诉调用方代码。

cues.en: This has some consequences.
cues.zh: 这会带来一些后果。

cues.en: There are certain things that the calling code cannot do anything about. So abstract machine corruption is a very simple example. Let's say you stack overflow,
cues.zh: 有些事情是调用方代码无能为力的。抽象机损坏就是个很简单的例子。比如说你栈溢出，

cues.en: not the online one, but, you know, actually really
cues.zh: 不是线上那个，而是，你知道，真的

cues.en: trying to make stack array of a billion or something. Oops. That didn't work.
cues.zh: 想创建一个十亿元素的栈数组之类的。哎呀，没成功。

cues.en: We treated that, think about it, if we treated that as an error code or an exception, report to the calling code.
cues.zh: 我们那样处理了，想想看，如果我们把它当作错误码或异常，上报给调用方代码。

cues.en: Well, first of all, what on earth is the calling code gonna do about it? It cannot programmatically recover because you may be in a corrupted state. If you run out of stack, you may actually not be in a consistent state anymore because you might have spilled some of your rights or corrupted memory.
cues.zh: 首先，调用方代码到底能拿它怎么办？它没法通过程序自动恢复，因为你可能已经处于损坏状态。如果栈耗尽，你可能实际上已经不再处于一致状态，因为你可能已经溢出了一些寄存器，或者破坏了内存。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: more to the point,
cues.zh: 更准确地说，

cues.en: if we did that, there would be no noexcept functions.
cues.zh: 如果那样做，就不会有 noexcept 函数了。

cues.en: Every function could throw.
cues.zh: 每个函数都可能抛出异常。

cues.en: Because any function could be the last one who's got one byte left on the stack when you try to call it.
cues.zh: 因为任何函数都可能是你调用它时，栈上只剩一个字节的那个函数。

cues.en: So this is not
cues.zh: 所以这不是

cues.en: the kind of error that we should report to the calling code because the calling code can't do anything about it. And if we tried, we would do damage to our programming model. We'd we'd be losing no except for all practical purposes, for example.
cues.zh: 那种我们应该报告给调用方的错误，因为调用方对此无能为力。而如果我们尝试报告，就会破坏我们的编程模型。比如，实际上我们就会失去 noexcept。

cues.en: So reporting that as a runtime error would really be a category error. It's not a runtime
cues.zh: 所以把它报告为运行时错误，其实真的是范畴错误。它不是运行时

cues.en: recoverable error.
cues.zh: 可恢复的错误。

cues.en: The same thing is true of a programming bug. So if we have an assertion in our program, or a precondition, or a post condition,
cues.zh: 程序 bug 也是一样。所以如果程序里有断言，或者前置条件、后置条件，

cues.en: and it's a statement about the expected state of our program,
cues.zh: 而它是在说明程序的预期状态，

cues.en: if we're using assertions in that way, then by definition, if we violate one, what does it mean?
cues.zh: 如果我们这样使用断言，那么按定义，一旦违反其中一个，意味着什么？

cues.en: It means the program is in a state that the code was not expecting and is not designed to recover from.
cues.zh: 意味着程序所处的状态，是代码没有预期到、也不是为从中恢复而设计的。

cues.en: Now there are techniques for... If you can partition your memory and have memory isolation and you have... You can throw away parts of your program and restart them. There are techniques to try to recover, but it's not by normal stack unwinding and and fixing things on the way back usually.
cues.zh: 现在有一些技术……如果你能划分内存并实现内存隔离，并且你有……你可以丢弃程序的一部分并重启它们。也有一些尝试恢复的技术，但通常不是通过正常的栈展开、在返回途中修复问题。

cues.en: It's by abandoning parts of possibly corrupt process and then resuming restarting.
cues.zh: 而是通过舍弃可能已损坏的进程部分，然后恢复并重启。

cues.en: These also should not be reported as runtime errors.
cues.zh: 这些也不应作为运行时错误报告。

cues.en: So out of bounds
cues.zh: 所以，越界

cues.en: should never
cues.zh: 绝不应该

cues.en: ever be an error code or an exception.
cues.zh: 成为错误码或异常。

cues.en: I know that that is gonna raise hackles with some of you because we're used to that. You'll say the standard library does that. I will show you that we talk to the standard library folks. I believe I have the polls in a few slides.
cues.zh: 我知道这会让你们有些人不满，因为我们习惯了。你们会说标准库就是这么做的。我会给你们看，我们和标准库的人聊过。我记得后面几页幻灯片里有投票结果。

cues.en: And they agree unanimously.
cues.zh: 他们一致同意。

cues.en: Yeah. That's a problem, and we're going to gradually migrate the standard library away
cues.zh: 是的。这是个问题，我们会逐步把标准库迁走

cues.en: from
cues.zh: 从

cues.en: basically the logic underscore error, which you might say is
cues.zh: 基本上就是 logic_error，你可能会说它

cues.en: inherently a logic error that shouldn't exist.
cues.zh: 本质上就是一个不该存在的逻辑错误。

cues.en: So here's our taxonomy.
cues.zh: 这是我们的分类体系。

cues.en: If we corrupt the abstract machine,
cues.zh: 如果我们破坏了抽象机，

cues.en: we need to stop. We might terminate doesn't mean right away. We might have some last ditch, you know, try to save some state before we terminate, but we can't really continue. We have to tell a syshop or somebody like that,
cues.zh: 我们就得停下来。我们可能会终止，但这不意味着要立刻终止。我们可能会在终止前做最后一搏，你知道，尝试保存一些状态，但我们其实没法继续下去。我们得告诉系统操作员或类似的人，

cues.en: and we are telling a human being because
cues.zh: 而我们是在告诉一个人，因为

cues.en: we need more space. The program failed, and you need to restart it.
cues.zh: 我们需要更多空间。程序失败了，你需要重启它。

cues.en: Category b, if there is a programming bug like an assert violation or a precondition violation.
cues.zh: B 类，如果存在编程错误，比如断言违规或前置条件违规。

cues.en: We express that using assertions,
cues.zh: 我们用断言来表达这一点，

cues.en: log checks, hopefully, contracts,
cues.zh: 日志检查，但愿还有契约，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 以及

cues.en: we tell also a human being, but this time we tell the programmer,
cues.zh: 我们也会告诉人，但这次告诉的是程序员：

cues.en: this is category b we want to come out in unit testing and system testing,
cues.zh: 这是 B 类，我们希望它在单元测试和系统测试中暴露出来，

cues.en: and we've identified a bug. Please go fix your bug.
cues.zh: 并且我们已经识别出一个 bug。请去修复你的 bug。

cues.en: Category b, we don't throw an exception because the program can't fix itself. Don't wanna tell the code. We wanna tell a human being.
cues.zh: B 类，我们不抛异常，因为程序没法自己修复。不想告诉代码，我们想告诉人。

cues.en: And finally we have recoverable error like host not found or no, that string did not contain an int. Please try again. And there we can throw an exception or use an error code, and we're reporting two different species to code.
cues.zh: 最后是可恢复错误，比如找不到主机，或者“不行，那个字符串里没有 int，请重试”。这时我们可以抛异常或使用错误码，我们是在向代码报告两种不同的东西。

cues.en: And the calling code should recover. So that's the taxonomy I want to to highlight because it's part of these four coordinated proposals. And it comes up when we talk about number two in particular, at number three.
cues.zh: 而调用代码应当能恢复。这就是我想强调的分类体系，因为它是这四项协同提案的一部分。特别是在讨论第二项、以及第三项时，它就会出现。

cues.en: So here are four coordinated proposals
cues.zh: 下面是四项协同提案

cues.en: which are about trying to solve the problems we identified at the top.
cues.zh: 它们旨在尝试解决我们在开头指出的问题。

cues.en: Each one of them could be its own paper,
cues.zh: 每一项都可以单独写成一篇论文，

cues.en: but I deliberately... Normally I encourage people to write narrower papers instead of big monolithic omnibus papers with a jumble of features. But
cues.zh: 但我有意……通常我会鼓励大家写范围更窄的论文，而不是写那种把各种特性杂乱堆在一起、大而全的巨无霸论文。但

cues.en: this isn't just a jumble. These are related.
cues.zh: 这并不只是杂糅。它们彼此相关。

cues.en: It could actually be a problem if we tried to solve these problems in isolation
cues.zh: 如果孤立地解决这些问题，实际上可能会出问题

cues.en: because we might get a local maxima.
cues.zh: 因为可能会陷入局部最优。

cues.en: And we might say, oh, here's a solution for a, and here's a solution for b, and for c, and for d. Then you stand back and we've standardized it and lived with it for ten years, we realized if we only had a time machine, how often have we said that? We'd go back and if we'd actually thought about a b c d together, we would have designed c a little differently,
cues.zh: 我们可能会说，哦，这是 a 的解决方案，这是 b 的，还有 c 和 d 的。然后退后一看，我们已经把它标准化并沿用了十年，才意识到，要是有一台时光机就好了——这话我们说过多少次？我们会回到过去，如果当初真的把 a、b、c、d 放在一起考虑，我们就会把 c 设计得稍有不同，

cues.en: which was just as efficient and just as useful, but now it doesn't cause a problem with integrating with the other three. So that's why I think it's important to look at these three together. And I think by the end of this section, I hope to convince you that if we do all of them,
cues.zh: 它同样高效、同样有用，但现在就不会和另外三个集成时出问题。所以我认为把这三个放在一起看很重要。我想在本节结束时，希望能说服你，如果我们把它们全都做了，

cues.en: the sum is greater... The whole is greater than the sum of the parts in terms of what we get to achieve.
cues.zh: 整体大于部分之和……从我们能取得的成果来看，整体确实大于各部分之和。

cues.en: So let's look at the first part of the proposal.
cues.zh: 那我们来看提案的第一部分。

cues.en: The first part of the proposal and the one that probably gets the most notice
cues.zh: 提案的第一部分，也可能是最受关注的部分

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 就是

cues.en: that we want to address the zero overhead of throwing exceptions.
cues.zh: 我们想解决抛出异常时的零开销问题。

cues.en: So inherently today, we are throwing objects of dynamic types
cues.zh: 所以如今从根本上说，我们抛出的是动态类型的对象

cues.en: that have to be type erased and dynamically allocated,
cues.zh: 这些对象必须做类型擦除并动态分配，

cues.en: and we catch using a form of RTTI.
cues.zh: 而捕获则使用的是某种 RTTI 形式。

cues.en: It's not dynamic cast that you can spell yourself, but it's an equivalent form that's built into the compiler that's basically a close cousin of dynamic cast that you can't spell yourself except as catch base reference.
cues.zh: 这不是你能自己写出的 dynamic_cast，而是编译器内建的一种等价形式，基本算是 dynamic_cast 的近亲；除了写成 catch 基类引用，你没法自己写出来。

cues.en: There's
cues.zh: 有

cues.en: a different kind of exception classification going on there. So the proposal is, well, if dynamic is the problem,
cues.zh: 一种不同的异常分类在进行。所以提案是：好吧，如果 dynamic 是问题，

cues.en: static may not be the answer, but it ought to be the first place you look.
cues.zh: static 可能不是答案，但它应该是你最先查看的地方。

cues.en: So let's try to see if static is the solution
cues.zh: 那我们来看看，静态方案是不是解法

cues.en: to this dynamic problem.
cues.zh: 针对这个动态问题。

cues.en: If we can throw values of a statically known type,
cues.zh: 如果我们能抛出静态已知类型的值，

cues.en: that means we can return it by value.
cues.zh: 那就意味着我们可以按值返回它。

cues.en: And if we catch by value,
cues.zh: 而如果我们按值捕获，

cues.en: that means we don't need to allocate and we don't do a heap allocation and we don't need to do RTTI because we know its type.
cues.zh: 那就意味着不需要分配，不做堆分配，也不需要做 RTTI，因为我们知道它的类型。

cues.en: It turns out that if you do it this way,
cues.zh: 事实证明，如果这样做，

cues.en: and this is basically the same as many languages have invented with a result type such as in Rust and Go,
cues.zh: 这基本上就和许多语言用结果类型实现的一样，比如 Rust 和 Go，

cues.en: Also,
cues.zh: 另外，

cues.en: the same thing boost expected does and outcome.
cues.zh: Boost.Expected 和 Outcome 也是这样做的。

cues.en: If you do that, the result is isomorphic to error codes. But one of the benefits of baking this into the language
cues.zh: 如果你这么做，结果就与错误码同构。但把这一机制内建到语言里的好处之一是

cues.en: is the language can basically overlap your success and failure returns and use the same registers or the same channel for either one because it's only gonna be one or the other. You're either gonna succeed and here you go, here's your int, or you're gonna fail and here's your error, right? And you can overlap those if you're the compiler.
cues.zh: 语言基本上可以让成功返回值和失败返回值重叠，用同一批寄存器或同一个通道来承载其中任意一个，因为最终只会有其中一种。你要么成功，那好，这是你的 int；要么失败，那这是你的 error，对吧？而如果你是编译器，你就可以让这两者重叠。

cues.en: And that could be a lot more efficient.
cues.zh: 这样能高效得多。

cues.en: The thing is we want this to be backward compatible. So because C plus plus already has dynamic exceptions,
cues.zh: 问题在于我们希望向后兼容。因为 C++ 已经有动态异常，

cues.en: we wanna keep all of the exception handling we have today in terms of the programming model, try, catch, throw.
cues.zh: 我们想保留现有的异常处理编程模型，也就是 try、catch、throw。

cues.en: But we want to be able to opt in,
cues.zh: 但我们希望能选择启用，

cues.en: therefore this is not a breaking change to say, oh, by the way, for my function, mister compiler,
cues.zh: 所以这不是破坏性变更：比如说，嘿，编译器先生，针对我的函数，

cues.en: please go and implement this using the fast path
cues.zh: 请用快速路径来实现它

cues.en: because I promise to only throw a std::error.
cues.zh: 因为我保证只抛出 std::error。

cues.en: So here's
cues.zh: 所以，它是这样

cues.en: how it would operate.
